flags.why: The visual sense of nom is more common as a standalone word than the caregiving sense.
Suy tưởng belongs to literary or reflective writing and would sound unusually elevated in casual conversation.
Quý tử means a son pampered by his family, without the specific attachment to his mother implied by 'mama's boy' ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/qu%C3%BD_t%E1%BB%AD)).
The Vietnamese describes a pampered son who cannot do anything for himself, without mentioning dependence on his mother.
flags.fix: He is a pampered son and can't do anything for himself.

flags.why: This disparaging sense commonly expresses contempt or mockery, which the colloquial tag does not convey ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/qu%C3%BD_t%E1%BB%AD)).
Learners are more likely to encounter ngoắc meaning 'beckon' today than meaning 'hang on a hook'.
